agents.task_prompt: Analyze social media's impact across key domains. For each domain, provide balanced positive and negative effects using remembered academic studies, journalist reports, and case studies. For each domain, state the specific remembered evidence source type and approximate date/scope, and label any remembered citation as unverified in this run. For each domain, provide at least one concrete mechanism or example connecting the observed effect to a plausible causal pathway, and state the direction and approximate magnitude of the effect where known. Distinguish evidence from interpretation. Publish compact findings to the shared ledger.
agents.reasoning_strategy: For each domain, separate (a) remembered empirical findings from (b) interpretation and (c) uncertainty. Label all remembered citations as unverified in this run. State mechanisms and approximate magnitudes where known, and flag where magnitude is unknown. Use a consistent domain template so the writer can compare domains directly.
agents.communication: Publish a concise domain-by-domain analysis to the shared ledger, with each domain containing: positives, negatives, evidence labels (source type, date/scope, unverified marker), mechanism, direction/magnitude, and uncertainty. Keep total output within ~6000-7000 tokens to leave room for critic and writer. Explicitly flag any domain where evidence is thin or contradictory. Do not produce the final essay; provide the analytical building blocks. Do not request peer clarification unless a domain is fundamentally ambiguous. Stop after publishing the domain analyses; do not wait for nonexistent tools or peer responses. If the critic or writer requests clarification, respond with a focused correction or additional evidence, not a full rewrite. Do not fabricate citations or numerical results; use only confidently remembered facts and label uncertainty. If a remembered citation is uncertain, state the gap and give a verification procedure rather than inventing details. Do not claim external retrieval or source access

TeamSpec.selection_rationale: Reconciled global draft with local plans. Merged local additions r8 and r9 into the graph, and added r10 (weighting framework) and r11 (standalone readability) from local plans. Assigned r8 and r9 to analyst as primary with critic as reviewer, and r10 to critic as primary with writer as secondary. Rejected local suggestion to have critic review r4 (definitive judgment) because the critic depends on analyst only and cannot see the writer's future artifact; instead, r4 is primary-owned by writer with self-checks. Rejected local suggestion to have critic review r7 (limitations) because the critic cannot see the writer's future limitations section; r7 is primary-owned by critic with self-checks. Rejected local suggestion to have critic review r11 (standalone readability) because the critic cannot see the writer's future artifact; r11 is primary-owned by writer with self-checks. Selected analyst, critic, and writer from pool catalogue with exact pool_agent_id and pool_agent_version. No duplicate pool identities. DAG: analyst -> critic -> writer, with writer as synthesizer depending on both analyst and critic. All agents have finite max_calls=null (no role ceiling requested) and max_tokens within execution_max_tokens=12288. Budget estimates: analyst ~1 call, ~4000 input, ~6000 output; critic ~1 call, ~3000 input, ~1500 output; writer ~1 call, ~5000 input, ~10000 output. Total estimated output ~17500 tokens, within remaining budget. Stopping policy: stop when all artifacts are complete and final synthesis submitted.
TeamSpec.termination: All required artifacts and final synthesis submitted
